messages.subject: Comparing MLGs obtained from study to MLGs in a database
parts: Hello! I'm currently trying to strain-type my experimentally-obtained MLGs (diploid, microsatellite), but I'd like to use a database of strains to compare my experimental MLGs to. Previously, I have used the 'mlg.filter' function to strain-type MLGs using Bruvo's distance, but I've never used the function to strain-type against a database. I'm hoping I can be pointed in the right direction for this. I did glance over the previous topics in this group but couldn't find what I'm looking for, so apologies if this has been answered elsewhere! Thank you very much!

messages.author: d4586792679cf1d0
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Comparing MLGs obtained from study to MLGs in a database
parts:
Hi Sydney,

I suggest you consider including all MLGs in the reference database as well as the new genotypes you just characterized to see how the unknowns cluster. Think fo the DB as background variation to classify your unknown MLGs. Does that help? We do something similar on our Phytophthora-ID database.

BTW, the genotyping technique has to be identical.

Best,
Nik
